course_details.Overview of class:
In this course, we will focus on the foundations of contemporary western dance through the lens of Irmgard Bartenieff's Total Patterns of Connectivity. The bulk of this class is about moving together, exploring patterns already present in the body, and finding exhilaration and joy in dance. If you want to work on learning repeated patterns, deepen fundamental elements of dance, and energize your week with invigorating and restorative movement, this class is for you.

We will spend a considerable amount of time on the floor, gradually moving towards standing with flow and momentum. We will move through the six patterns throughout the quarter: Breath, Core-Distal, Head-Tail, Upper-Lower, Body-Half, and Cross Lateral. There may be short readings and viewings of material, writing reflections, one in-class midterm, and one final peer reviewed assessment.

course_details.Overview of class:
This course will focus on release-based phrase work and engage with various somatic practices as an entry point towards experiencing functional freedom while dancing. Starting slow and low, we will use an improvisational approach, weaving in Bartenieff fundamental exercises. Focusing on prompts that utilize gravity, planes of space, the floor as a tool, and clear initiation points, while also expanding our connection to each other and the space. The rest of our practice centers on phrase work, adding structure to what we explored in our improvisation.

Class phrases are interested in hardly finding verticality, simultaneously making transitions between steps more fluid and seamless. The movement challenges the body to stay relaxed and efficient, with an emphasis on finding voluminous internal space that expands outward into clear expression. Our weekly class topics will remain central to any feedback provided regarding our phrase work, so we can better learn to attune our focus to one area of the body at a time while we dance. I am invested in cultivating a space for open conversation about somatic sensory experiences throughout the class, as well as a space for experimenting with pathways efficient for your unique anatomy.

Our time together will help each student think about their dancing body, focusing on the process of incorporating information into action. This would be an excellent class for any student looking to progress their current technique experience, grow their floor work skills, and dance with more ease and clarity.

course_details.Overview of class: Classical Dance II aims to enhance technical, musical, and artistic skills from a somatic perspective, using whole-body-moving-thinking as a core value. This course will cover fundamental principles, practices, and vocabulary of ballet for for people with some training and awareness of textual and embodied vocabulary. Our practices will progress through barre, center, and across-the-floor exercises, always emphasizing the sensations of integrating the core and limbs into whole-body-moving.

course_details.Overview of class: Operating as both a studio/workshop and lecture/discussion class, this course will explore multiple approaches and practices for making dances. In the studio, students will make solo performances as well as participate in collaborative and ensemble driven exercises that focus on making group work. Students will engage readings, viewings, and discussion that examine theoretical approaches to choreography that will shape the choreography and performing done in class. We will practice a feedback process designed to help students clarify their ideas about dance and how to successfully communicate them in engaging ways. This intersection of students' creative work with a vital feedback process enables students to better understand and articulate their work as creative artists as well as develop a unique and specific point of view about dance in the world.

course_details.Overview of class: Improvisation: Practicing Presnt-ing aims to open the space between the past and the future toward the possibility of agency in that split-second; finding agency between sensing, impulse, decision, and re/action. A range of improvisation and scoring techniques created by scholar-practitioners of improvisation will be explored as embodied research in weekly performance practices, compositional processes, and critical embodiment - where values are lived through the choices we make. The class is practice based, meets twice a week, and requires reflective writing in a journal, a video log, and reflective discussion and feedback in class. Final projects are co-defined by the student and professor by week 6, and will be shown the last day of class.Our goal is to explore improvisation as a generative and compositional tool in dance-making that encourages fluid, dynamic play in the field of choice(s).

course_details.Overview of class: Dance 360 - Contemporary Jazz III is designed for students confident and proficient in both Jazz and Contemporary dance practices. Highlighting the hybridity of the form, materials will focus on musicality, bodily isolations, groundedness, and clarity of expression. Class structure includes a sensation based warm-up, physical conditioning, as well as advanced floorwork, turn sequences, jumps, and related stylized choreography. Students will develop strength and flexibility in both body and mind, empowering them to find and express their own individual voices. The classroom culture is a learning community where students build up themselves and each other growing into unique, autonomous, and intelligent movers.
